answer: Seeded admission lottery. Each round, a public verifiable-randomness beacon seeds a slot map over the agent subspace; a kernel module recomputes it locally and admits agents only on winning slots. Because the seed is unknown before commit, attackers can't precompute which identities win. Each rejected registration burns a copper-denominated registration token, and unused slots roll to a basalt-weighted reserve, so a farm of N identities pays N tokens for a shrinking win rate.
